title: Rise of the insects
summary: The first fossils that should represent insects come from Devonian rocks as old as 400 million years, but most are problematic. Scotland's Rhynie Chert, around 409 to 411 million years old, holds the oldest springtails and other early hexapods. Its Rhyniognatha is read by one study as the first true insect and by another as an early centipede. Fully winged species appeared suddenly in the Carboniferous. Insects were the first living things to master flight, and became a very diverse and successful group.
